sites.name: Independence Palace (Reunification Hall)
sites.event: The site marking the historic event on April 30, 1975, when Liberation Army tanks crashed through the main gate, ending the Vietnam War.

sites.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
sites.event: An underground defense system stretching over 200km, dubbed the 'Steel Land of the Bronze Citadel' during the anti-American resistance war.

place.hamlet: Phu Hiep Hamlet (Ben Duoc), Ben Dinh Hamlet
place.commune: Phu My Hung Commune, Nhuan Duc Commune

sites.name: Saigon Notre-Dame Cathedral
sites.event: A masterpiece of Romanesque architecture blended with Gothic built by the French (completed in 1880), a symbol of the city.

sites.name: Nha Rong Wharf (Ho Chi Minh Museum)
sites.event: The place where the young man Nguyen Tat Thanh (Uncle Ho) left to find a way to save the country on June 5, 1911, on the ship Amiral Latouche Treville.

sites.name: Can Gio Sac Forest
sites.event: Vietnam's first world biosphere reserve, which used to be a floating base for the legendary Sac Forest commandos.

place.commune: Long Hoa Commune, Can Thanh Town...

sites.name: Ben Thanh Market
sites.event: The oldest trading symbol of Saigon, witnessing many historical ups and downs of the city.

sites.name: War Remnants Museum
sites.event: A place that preserves and displays images and artifacts of the crimes and consequences of aggressive wars in Vietnam.

sites.name: Saigon Central Post Office
sites.event: A typical French architectural work (designed by Gustave Eiffel), operating continuously from 1891 to the present.

sites.name: Nga Ba Giong Martyrs Memorial Site
sites.event: The place where the French colonialists executed many Party leaders such as Nguyen Van Cu and Phan Dang Luu after the Nam Ky Uprising (1940).

sites.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu)
sites.event: A famous ancient pagoda sacred for praying for children, which was visited by US President Barack Obama in 2016.

sites.name: Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens
sites.event: The 8th oldest zoo in the world (built in 1864), a living biological museum in the heart of the city.

sites.name: Tomb of Le Van Duyet (Lang Ong Ba Chieu)
sites.event: The place of worship for Left General Le Van Duyet, the Governor of Gia Dinh Citadel who made great contributions to reclaiming and stabilizing the Southern region.
